summary: Step-back procedure request: mixed-precision optimizer + KV prefetch causing cost/latency variance for BrightLedger
description:
Issue summary: BrightLedger reports a sudden increase in per-token billing and intermittent P95 latency spikes after enabling a mixed-precision optimizer profile (adaptive-mix) combined with tenant-scoped KV prefetch. Impact: higher cost, increased tail latency for interactive routes (chat endpoints), and customer urgency to revert with minimal disruption.

Observed at ~2026-03-09 22:00 UTC when tenant opt experiment was promoted to 100% for BrightLedger. Customer requests a safe, staged step-back plan and assistance to execute it on Dedicated capacity without broad service disruption.
steps_to_reproduce:
1) Enable optimizer profile 'adaptive-mix' for BrightLedger tenant (tenant_id: brightledger-prod)
2) Turn on kv_prefetch=true and set batch_max_tokens=4096 in optimizer policy
3) Send standard chat traffic (session length 200-600 tokens, many concurrent short sessions)
4) Observe tail latency and token accounting change in console and billing reports

Note: Reproduction tied to tenant production traffic pattern; can be reproduced on a staging replica with a sampled traffic replay.
logs_and_metrics_snapshot:
Console traces: spike in kv-cache eviction rate at 2026-03-09T22:03:10Z; cache hit ratio dropped from 93% -> 56% for tenant. Serving runtime logs: increased decoder wait times and queue length; per-request kernel times show higher GPU decode stalls. Billing delta: estimated token cost +18% week-on-week for tenant routes after change.
Links: /console/tenant/brightledger/metrics?from=2026-03-09T21:30Z&to=2026-03-09T23:30Z, /logs/query?query=tenant:brightledger+AND+kv_eviction
investigation_notes:
Initial hypothesis: the mixed-precision quant profile (q4_0-like) reduces per-token compute but changes memory layout and increases KV cache pressure for sessions with many short, interleaved prefixes. Combined with aggressive kv_prefetch the runtime is preloading incompatible cache entries, causing frequent evictions and cache misses. This increases decoder work per request and observed tail latency. Also discovered batch_max_tokens was raised simultaneously which increased queueing for short interactive sessions.
Evidence: correlation between config change timestamp and eviction/hitrate drop; heap and profiler dumps show larger KV index churn; switching traffic to fp16 model reduced P95 immediately in a controlled test.
customer_impact: High: BrightLedger (finance SaaS) reports degraded end-user experience for chat features and expects cost regressions to be addressed. Dedicated contract includes latency SLOs. They require step-back with minimal session loss and prefer a 10-30 minute window for the operation.
workaround_recommendation:
Short-term mitigations (can be executed immediately):
- Set tenant optimizer feature flag 'adaptive-mix' -> 'hold' (effective immediately) to stop further profile toggles.
- Temporarily disable kv_prefetch for tenant (kv_prefetch=false) to reduce eviction churn.
- Reduce batch_max_tokens to 1024 to lower queuing for interactive routes.
- Route critical chat route to fallback fp16 model (gptish-13b-fp16) with 100% or 90/10 traffic-split depending on tolerance.
These steps reduce cost surge and P95 without full rollout rollback. Monitor for 10-15 minutes and escalate to snapshot restore if no improvement.
proposed_step_back_plan:
Phase 0 - Preparation (5-10 min): capture live optimizer snapshot for tenant (optimizer_snapshot_id) and take traffic snapshot in console; notify SRE and customer success.
Phase 1 - Soft hold (0-5 min): apply 'adaptive-mix' -> 'hold' and set kv_prefetch=false on tenant config. Observe metrics for 10 min.
Phase 2 - Minimal change (5-10 min): lower batch_max_tokens to 1024 and optionally route 20% traffic to gptish-13b-fp16 for safety. Observe for another 10 min.
Phase 3 - Snapshot restore (if Phase 1/2 insufficient): restore previous stable optimizer snapshot from 2026-03-07 config with snapshot restore API; then roll traffic back off the quant profile fully.
Phase 4 - Post-check (10-30 min): run latency/cost verification checklist and hold for 30 minutes before closing.
All steps include quick rollback commands and are reversible; aim for <30 min customer-impact window.
manual_commands_and_playbook_links:
Commands (ops console / cli):
- Hold optimizer: rwctl optimizer set-feature --tenant brightledger-prod --feature adaptive-mix --state hold
- Disable kv prefetch: rwctl config set --tenant brightledger-prod --key optimizer.kv_prefetch --value false
- Adjust batch_max_tokens: rwctl config set --tenant brightledger-prod --key optimizer.batch_max_tokens --value 1024
- Route traffic to fallback: rwctl routing set --tenant brightledger-prod --route /chat --model gptish-13b-fp16 --split 90:10
Snapshot restore API: POST /api/internal/optimizer/snapshots/restore with body {"tenant":"brightledger-prod","snapshot_id":"<snapshot>"} (runbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/SERV/optimizer-snapshot-restore)
Note: Confirm commands with SRE on-call before executing; commands require dedicated-admin role.
